title: Albany council aims to set tax levy by Thursday as budget vote nears Nov. 30 deadline - WRGB

 Albany residents could soon see higher property taxes as city leaders race to close a growing budget gap ahead of a Nov. 30 deadline to pass a budget.
 A tax levy number hasn't been set yet, and Mayor Dr. Dorcey Applyrs’ current proposal includes a 15 percent increase. “My administration has been clear. We are holding the line in preserving public safety and investing in public safety,” Applyrs said.
 The Common Council is looking for ways to reduce the increase. Ward 6 Councilor Deirdre Brodie said the council is reviewing revenue assumptions it does not believe will come in as projected.
 “The opportunity to look at taking out certain things on the revenue side that we just don't think are going to materialize to the tune of about $16.7 million. And then bringing the property tax cap increase to, below the rate that would require an override,” Brodie said.
 Residents raised concerns Monday night about the overall budget and the impact of any tax increase. One resident urged city leaders: “Do not, I repeat, do not override any version of the tax cap that's being proposed.”
 City officials are also facing questions about Albany’s financial standing after its S & P rating was lowered in July from A-plus to A. A Times Union article raised concerns that it could be downgraded again.
 Applyrs said her administration has been in contact with the rating agency. “My administration, the treasurer's office. We've been having those candid conversations with S & P, and we want to assure them that as a city leadership team, we have the city's finances under control. We are working to address a historic financial crisis,” she said.
 Albany’s city treasurer, responding to questions about the downgrade, said in part: “The rating doesn't necessarily affect the ability to borrow as much as how the markets view the City and its financial prospects overall. We were encouraged by this sale that the rate we achieved was better than we expected.” He also said the city could expect high interest rates in the future.
 The city’s finance committee is scheduled to meet Thursday, with the treasurer expected to attend and answer questions. Brodie said she expects a direct discussion. “I think having conversations face to face are much more productive than talking about other people's social media. So I'm looking forward to a healthy conversation in person,” she said.
 The council plans to establish a tax levy percentage by the end of Thursday’s meeting. A City Council meeting to pass the budget is scheduled for Nov. 30.
